content:
**P289-STACK-MERGE-ORDER — INSTANCE TWO. A stacked child PR merged into its parent's branch AFTER the parent already merged, orphaning the child's content off the integration branch. Prose warnings did not prevent it; a repo setting does.**

**The failure shape.** In a stack, child PR B targets parent PR A's branch. When A merges into the integration branch, A's branch becomes dead. If B is then merged WITHOUT retargeting, it merges into that dead branch — GitHub reports B as MERGED, the PR turns purple, every check is green, and B's content never reaches the integration branch. The signal and the reality disagree, and nothing surfaces the disagreement.

**Instance one (#287 / #288 / corrected by #289).** H1-5b/5c shipped stacked. Both merged, in the wrong order, and the H1-5c board content was orphaned. Corrected by a corrective PR.

**Instance two (#298 / #299 / corrected by #300, 2026-07-21).** #298 (D2 PR3a) merged into feature/v2.0.0 at 22:50:59Z. #299 (D2 PR3b) merged TWENTY SECONDS LATER, at 22:51:19Z, into feat/issue-259-d2-pr3a-net-parity-guard — the already-dead parent. PR3b's three held corrections never reached feature/v2.0.0, which was left in a strictly worse state than either PR alone: the exemption machinery and the (c') guard were live, WITHOUT the audited-tip anchoring, WITHOUT the SIG drift-guard, and — most dangerous — WITHOUT the MINOR 2 fix, so the error-swallowing git() helper stayed live and any transient git failure read as a governance PASS.

**Why the warning failed.** The lesson from instance one was recorded in engram AND written explicitly into BOTH PR bodies, including the retarget instruction. It still happened. Comments, PR bodies and memory are INVISIBLE at the merge button. This is the same category error as R297-APPROVE-READS-AS-GO, one level down: a gate that is not mechanized is not a gate, it is an intention.

**The mechanical prevention (enabled 2026-07-21).** Repo setting "Automatically delete head branches" (delete_branch_on_merge: true). When the parent merges, GitHub deletes its branch and AUTO-RETARGETS every open child PR to the parent's base. The wrong target ceases to exist, so the failure shape becomes impossible rather than merely discouraged.

**Detection, if it ever recurs.** Do not trust the PR's MERGED badge — ask git:
    git merge-base --is-ancestor <child-head-sha> origin/<integration-branch>
NO means orphaned. Confirm by grepping the integration branch for a symbol the child introduced:
    git show origin/<integration-branch>:<path> | rg -c <symbol>

**Recovery is a merge, not a reconstruction.** The parent's branch still exists and now CONTAINS the orphaned merge, so a corrective PR from that branch to the integration branch restores everything as one reviewable unit. Review it by TREE IDENTITY rather than re-reading the diff: if git rev-parse <branch>^{tree} equals the already-verified commit's tree, the merge introduced zero content and prior verification carries over by sha. In instance two both trees were 6d8edd96d562739e8be2d1b765d32e5e6b0fed12 and git diff between them was empty.

**Ordering rule when a stack must be merged by hand.** Merge the parent, then RETARGET the child to the integration branch and confirm the base changed BEFORE merging it. Never merge a stack back-to-back on the assumption that retargeting is automatic unless delete_branch_on_merge is enabled and verified.
